name: workspace.listFolder
title: List folder
summary: The folders and links, and on request the files, in the folder of a typed path: the text up to its last separator (`/`, and `\` on Windows) names the folder, the rest is the typed name. A relative path is resolved from the workspace root on every access, also on the command line; with `absolute` the path must be absolute, and `~` stands for the home folder. The path is checked by its text first: a UNC, device or NT path, a path on the current drive, a Windows device name, NUL or more than 4096 characters gives `invalid` without any file-system call. Through the API and the MCP server the folder must lie inside the repositories of the workspace (SR-142). Only the entries of the folder are read: no link is resolved, so a link is listed by its name. Known limit: where the file system gives no entry type with the names (NFS without readdirplus, some FUSE file systems, XFS without ftype), each entry is looked at once with lstat, never through a link, and outside the 1 s bound.

path.description: The typed path, up to the name being typed (`~/pro`, `out/`, `C:\Work\sp`). A plain text, not a `localPath`: it is taken as typed, with its separator at the end.

files.description: Also list the files (for an argument that takes a file); folders and links are always listed.

absolute.description: Take only an absolute path, with `~` and `~/…` for the home folder ("Open workspace", SR-131); without it `~` is an ordinary name, as the commands resolve a path argument.

folder.description: The folder listed, absolute and normalised, without a separator at its end except at the root. Missing when the path is `invalid`.

name.description: The typed name: the text after the last separator. Names that start with "." are listed only when it starts with ".".
The name as the file system spells it.

kind.description: folder, file, or link: a symbolic link, and on Windows any reparse point (junctions, OneDrive and Cloud Files placeholders, deduplicated files, app execution aliases); its target is not looked at.

entries.description: The entries, folders and links first, then files, each by the code units of the NFC form of the name. Other entries (sockets, devices) are left out. Empty with a `problem`.

problem.description: Why there are no entries: the folder does not exist (`missing`), cannot be read or gave no answer within 1 s (`unreadable`, also when the path names a file), or the path is refused by its text (`invalid`).

truncated.description: The folder has more than 50,000 matching entries; folders and links come first.
